title: Big Bend National Park: Desert canyons, hot springs & dark skies
description: A solo adventure through one of America's most remote and dramatic national parks. Big Bend in late February offers perfect hiking weather, uncrowded trails, and some of the darkest night skies in North America.

days.title: Chisos Basin & Lost Mine Trail
days.description: Arrive at the park, conquer the best ridgeline hike, and settle into the only lodge inside Big Bend.

activities.name: Panther Junction Visitor Center
activities.description: Start here to get oriented. Rangers can advise on current trail conditions, wildlife sightings, and water availability. Grab a park map and check the ranger program schedule. One of Big Bend's best hikes — a 4.8-mile round trip gaining 1,100 feet to a panoramic ridgeline view of the Chisos Mountains and the Sierra del Carmen in Mexico. February weather makes this ideal with comfortable temps and clear visibility.

activities.name: Window View Trail
activities.description: After Lost Mine, take the easy 0.3-mile Window View Trail for a framed view of the desert floor through a V-shaped gap in the mountains. Perfect for golden hour photos. If you have energy, the full Window Trail (5.6 mi RT) descends into the canyon.

activities.name: Stargazing at Chisos Basin
activities.description: Big Bend is an International Dark Sky Park — one of the least light-polluted areas in North America. Step outside after dinner and look up. The Milky Way is breathtaking in February's crisp, clear skies.

days.neighborhoods: Ross Maxwell Drive · Santa Elena · Terlingua
days.title: Santa Elena Canyon & Terlingua
days.description: Drive the park's most scenic road, hike into a 1,500-foot canyon, and end the day in a legendary ghost town.

activities.name: Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive
activities.description: This 30-mile one-way drive is the crown jewel of Big Bend scenic roads. Stop at Sam Nail Ranch (old homestead with bird-filled oasis), Sotol Vista Overlook for sweeping desert panoramas, and Tuff Canyon for a quick geology lesson.

activities.name: Santa Elena Canyon Trail
activities.description: The most iconic hike in Big Bend. A 1.5-mile round trip that follows the Rio Grande into a canyon with 1,500-foot limestone walls towering on both sides — Mexico on your left, Texas on your right. You'll cross Terlingua Creek at the start (usually dry in February). The trail ends at a sandy beach perfect for a quiet moment. Stop at this old frontier trading post near Santa Elena Canyon. The Castolon Store (La Harmonia) is one of the oldest adobe structures in the park. Grab an ice cream or cold drink.

activities.name: Terlingua Ghost Town at Sunset
activities.description: Wander the ruins of this old mercury mining town as the sun sets over the Chisos Mountains. The cemetery on the hill is hauntingly beautiful at golden hour. This is the heart of Big Bend's quirky community — artists, drifters, and desert lovers.

days.neighborhoods: Hot Springs · Boquillas · Rio Grande Village
days.title: Hot Springs, Boquillas & Farewell
days.description: Soak in a natural hot spring, hike a dramatic canyon, and take a rowboat to Mexico for the most unique lunch of your life.

activities.name: Hot Springs Historic Trail
activities.description: A 1-mile round trip to a natural hot spring right on the Rio Grande. The stone-walled pool sits at about 105°F year-round — perfect for a morning soak with views of the river and Mexico. Check out the old motel ruins and pictographs along the trail.

activities.name: Boquillas Canyon Trail
activities.description: A 1.4-mile round trip to a massive canyon where the Rio Grande cuts through limestone. Less crowded than Santa Elena but equally dramatic. Views of the tiny Mexican village of Boquillas del Carmen across the river. One of the most unique border crossings in the US — take a $5 rowboat across the Rio Grande to this tiny Mexican village. Bring your passport and cash. Open Wed–Sun.

activities.name: Depart Big Bend
activities.description: Head north out of the park via US-385. If you have time, stop in Marathon (90 min north) for a coffee at the Gage Hotel — a beautifully restored 1927 hotel and a West Texas landmark. Fill up on gas before leaving the area. Safe travels!
